entries.title: Free Auto just works
entries.body: Free Atlarix Auto runs your first message with no key and no question. Sub-agents finish their part, the chat keeps up with long answers, and in the CLI you can click to edit.

entries.title: Sessions that review each other
entries.body: Sessions see each other's messages where they land and review each other's requests. Questions come with described, multi-pick options. In the CLI, ctrl+s sends what you queued now.

entries.title: Sessions that talk to each other
entries.body: Fork a session, send it a task, set its mode and model, review its plan, and get notified when it finishes. Cross-session messaging works across the app, CLI, VS Code and any ACP editor.

entries.title: Your keys and MCP servers, everywhere
entries.body: Every API key is checked with its provider, and MCP servers from Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code are found with an Add button. The editor extension is redesigned.

entries.title: Atlarix in VS Code, Cursor, Kiro and Windsurf
entries.body: Install the Atlarix extension and the whole agent runs in your editor: every mode, your models and keys, and edits you approve in the editor's own diff.

entries.title: Atlarix in your editor
entries.body: Use Atlarix inside Zed, JetBrains IDEs and VS Code: point your editor at `atlarix acp`. Edits and commands still wait for your OK.

entries.title: Hand a browser task to Chrome
entries.body: Your terminal or app session can now send the Atlarix Chrome extension a job; click its icon to start it and steer it as it works. New accounts get double the free allowance in week one.

entries.title: The app is free, and skills live in your repo
entries.body: Every feature is on every plan; Atlarix Core inference is what's metered. Skills are now markdown files in your project's .atlarix/skills/, and a cancelled turn bills only what it produced.

entries.title: Talk to Atlarix while it is working
entries.body: A message you type mid-turn now reaches the turn that is running, instead of waiting for it to end. Type as many as you like — each one is cancellable until it is picked up.

entries.title: Atlarix Core 1 is now GLM 5.3
entries.body: Core 1 moved to GLM 5.3 — same 1M context, same price, and deep thinking scales to what the model supports. Nothing to install; it is already live.

entries.title: Your plan updates when you come back
entries.body: Upgrading happens in a browser, so Atlarix now re-checks your plan every time you return to the window instead of only after it had been idle.

entries.title: A usage bar that reads as a percentage
entries.body: Settings shows how much of this month's included usage you have spent, and leads with the credit you bought. Your account page now separates Atlarix from Atlarix Reviewer.
